definition_zh: 纯粹的；陡峭的；极薄的；完全地
definition_en: complete and nothing else, very steep, very thin and transparent, or completely
core_image: 一面几乎垂直的岩壁，从水面直插天空
scene: 悬崖从海面陡然升起。The cliff rises sheer from the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 sheer 是「陡峭的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：悬崖从海面陡然升起。

senses.title: Complete
senses.definition: used to emphasize that something is nothing but what is stated
senses.definitionCN: 强调某事物完全是所说的那样
senses.example: It was sheer luck that we met.
senses.why: This is the most common modern use.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最常见的用法。

senses.title: Very steep
senses.definition: rising almost straight up
senses.definitionCN: 几乎垂直升起的
senses.example: The cliff rises sheer from the sea.
senses.why: A sheer face has no slope to hold on to.
senses.whyCN: 陡壁没有任何可攀附的斜坡。

senses.title: Very thin
senses.definition: thin, light, and almost transparent
senses.definitionCN: 薄、轻且近乎透明的
senses.example: She wore a sheer silk scarf.
senses.exampleCN: 她戴了一条极薄的丝巾。
senses.why: Thin cloth lets light through like clear air.
senses.whyCN: 薄布像清澈空气一样透光。

senses.title: Completely
senses.definition: used as an adverb meaning completely
senses.definitionCN: 作副词表示完全地
senses.example: The door was sheer impossible to open.
senses.why: Pure emphasis turns the adjective into an adverb.
senses.whyCN: 纯粹的强调使形容词转为副词。

intro.en: Sheer joins an Old English word for bright and clear with a Norse word for steep.
intro.cn: sheer 把古英语中表示明亮清澈的词与古诺尔斯语中表示陡峭的词合在一起。

items.en: Scir meant bright, clear, or pure.
items.cn: scir 意为明亮、清澈或纯净。

items.en: Skaerr meant clear or clean.
items.cn: skaerr 意为清澈或洁净。

items.en: Schere described thin, clear cloth.
items.cn: schere 形容轻薄透明的布。

items.en: Sheer described a steep, unbroken face.
items.cn: sheer 形容陡峭完整的崖面。

items.en: Sheer became an intensifier meaning complete.
items.cn: sheer 成为表示「完全」的强调词。

note.en: Sheer is compared with similar-looking words and with words for purity and steepness.
note.cn: 把 sheer 与形近词以及表示纯粹和陡峭的词作比较。

entries.definition: to cut wool from a sheep

normalIntro.en: Sheer is what is unstoppable and unmixed: a clean cliff, thin cloth, pure luck.
normalIntro.cn: sheer 是无法阻挡、没有混杂的东西：干净的崖壁、薄布、纯粹的运气。

normal.en: It was sheer luck.
The wall is sheer rock.
She wore a sheer dress.
The sheer size amazed us.
normal.cn: 其规模之大让我们惊叹。

normal.en: By sheer chance we met.

abstract.en: A sheer face offers no place to stop.
abstract.cn: 陡壁不提供任何停留之处。

abstract.en: Thin cloth shows what clear air hides.
abstract.cn: 薄布显露出清澈空气所隐藏的东西。

abstract.en: Pure luck looks like skill from outside.
abstract.cn: 纯粹的运气从外面看像技巧。

examples.en: The cliff rises sheer from the sea.
It was sheer luck that we met.
She wore a sheer silk scarf.
examples.cn: 她戴了一条极薄的丝巾。

dict_mnemonic.text: sheer 兼有「清澈纯净」与「陡直」两源，核心义「没有任何混杂或折角」。

root: 由古英语 scir（明亮清澈）与古诺尔斯语 skaerr（纯净）汇合，核心义「纯粹、陡直」。

sensesIntro.en: Sheer means complete, very steep, very thin, or completely.
sensesIntro.cn: sheer 意为纯粹的、陡峭的、极薄的或完全地。

core.en: Nothing mixed in and nothing in the way.
core.cn: 没有混杂，也没有遮挡。

branches.en: Luck with nothing else added.
A face with no slope.
Cloth that lets light through.
Emphasis with no reservation.
Purity and emphasis share one word.
branches.cn: 纯粹与强调共用一个词。

intro.en: Sheer has a small family of degree and steepness.
intro.cn: sheer 有一个表示程度与陡峭的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Sheer has no Latin ancestor; Latin merus, pure, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: sheer 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 merus（纯粹的）只是语义对应词。

items.example: This is the sheerest part of the cliff.
The sheerness of the rock surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 岩石的陡峭让我们惊讶。

items.example: The boat sheered away from the rocks.
The ship kept sheering in the wind.

definition_en: a hard outer case, an explosive projectile, to remove such a case, or to attack with shells
core_image: 一只海螺壳贴在耳边，里面传出海的声音
scene: 她在沙滩上捡到一个贝壳。She found a shell on the beach.
sceneCN: 这里 shell 是「壳」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她在沙滩上捡到一个贝壳。

senses.title: Hard case
senses.definition: the hard outer covering of an egg, nut, or sea creature
senses.definitionCN: 蛋、坚果或海洋生物的坚硬外壳
senses.example: She found a shell on the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 她在沙滩上捡到一个贝壳。
senses.why: This is the basic natural sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的自然义项。

senses.title: Projectile
senses.definition: a metal case filled with explosive fired from a gun
senses.definitionCN: 从火炮发射的装填炸药的金属弹体
senses.example: An old shell was found in the field.
senses.exampleCN: 田里发现了一枚旧炮弹。
senses.why: A metal case protects what is inside, as a shell does.
senses.whyCN: 金属外壳像壳一样保护内部。

senses.title: Remove the case
senses.definition: to remove the shell from nuts or seafood
senses.definitionCN: 去掉坚果或海鲜的壳
senses.example: They shelled the peas.
senses.why: The noun became a verb of removing a case.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为去壳的动词。

senses.title: Bombard
senses.definition: to attack a place with explosive shells
senses.definitionCN: 用爆炸弹体攻击某地
senses.example: The town was shelled for hours.
senses.why: The projectile became the action of firing it.
senses.whyCN: 弹体转化为发射它的动作。

intro.en: Shell comes from Old English scell, a hard outer covering.
intro.cn: shell 源自古英语 scell，意为坚硬的外壳。

items.en: The root named a hard covering.
items.cn: 这个词根指坚硬的覆盖物。

items.en: Scell meant the shell of an egg or nut.
items.cn: scell 指蛋壳或坚果壳。

items.en: Shell named the case of sea creatures.
items.cn: shell 指海洋生物的外壳。

items.en: Shell named an explosive projectile.
items.cn: shell 指爆炸性弹体。

items.en: The verb meant to remove a shell or to bombard.
items.cn: 动词形式意为去壳或炮击。

note.en: Shell is compared with similar-looking words and with words for coverings.
note.cn: 把 shell 与形近词以及表示外壳的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Shell is a hard outside that protects a soft inside, from eggs to warships.
normalIntro.cn: shell 是保护柔软内部的坚硬外层，从鸡蛋到军舰都一样。

normal.en: The egg shell cracked.
She collects sea shells.
They shelled the nuts.
The building was shelled.
The turtle pulled into its shell.

abstract.en: A shell is a boundary that can be left behind.
abstract.cn: 壳是可以被留下的边界。

abstract.en: Protection and weapon share one word.
abstract.cn: 保护与武器共用一个词。

abstract.en: What is empty inside is still a shell.
abstract.cn: 里面空了，仍然是个壳。

examples.en: She found a shell on the beach.
examples.cn: 她在沙滩上捡到一个贝壳。

examples.en: They shelled the peas.
The town was shelled for hours.

dict_mnemonic.text: shell 源自古英语 scell（硬壳），核心义「包住内部的硬外层」，由蛋壳、贝壳引申为弹壳与炮击。

root: 源自古英语 scell（硬壳），核心义「保护内部的坚硬外层」。

sensesIntro.en: Shell means a hard case, a projectile, to remove a case, or to bombard.
sensesIntro.cn: shell 意为硬壳、炮弹、剥壳或炮击。

core.en: A hard outside around a softer inside.
core.cn: 包住柔软内部的坚硬外层。

branches.en: A natural hard covering.
A metal case filled with explosive.
The act of taking a shell off.
The act of firing shells.
The case and the attack share one word.
branches.cn: 弹壳与炮击共用一个词。

intro.en: Shell builds words for animals, weapons, and protection.
intro.cn: shell 构成表示动物、武器和防护的词。

latinIntro.en: Shell has no Latin ancestor; Latin testa, a shell, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shell 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 testa（壳）只是语义对应词。

items.meaning: bombarded or removed from a shell
items.example: Shelled nuts are easier to eat.

items.meaning: a sea animal with a shell
the hard case of a nut
items.example: In a nutshell, the plan works.

definition_en: a place that protects from weather or danger, or to protect someone or find protection
core_image: 暴雨中，几个人挤在公交站小小的顶棚下
scene: 他们在一棵大树下避雨。They sheltered under a large tree.
sceneCN: 这里 shelter 是「躲避」（第 3 个义项）；句意：他们在一棵大树下避雨。

senses.title: Place of protection
senses.definition: a place that protects people from weather or danger
senses.definitionCN: 保护人们免受天气或危险的地方
senses.example: The bus stop was a poor shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 公交站是个简陋的避雨处。
senses.why: This is the basic noun sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的名词义项。

senses.title: To protect
senses.definition: to protect someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 保护某人或某物
senses.example: The wall shelters the garden from wind.
senses.why: The noun became a verb of protecting.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为保护的动词。

senses.title: To find cover
senses.definition: to go to a place that gives protection
senses.definitionCN: 到能提供保护的地方去
senses.example: They sheltered under a large tree.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一棵大树下避雨。
senses.why: The same verb can describe the person protected.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词也可描述受保护的人。

senses.title: Condition of safety
senses.definition: the state of being protected
senses.definitionCN: 受到保护的状态
senses.example: They found shelter from the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 他们找到了躲避暴风雨的地方。
senses.why: A shelter is both a place and a condition.
senses.whyCN: shelter 既是地点也是状态。

intro.en: Shelter comes from Middle English sheltron, a troop or phalanx of soldiers.
intro.cn: shelter 源自中古英语 sheltron，意为士兵的方阵。

items.en: Scildtruma meant a shield troop.
items.cn: scildtruma 意为持盾的队伍。

items.en: Sheltron meant a body of soldiers.
items.cn: sheltron 意为一支士兵队伍。

items.en: Shelter came to mean protection.
items.cn: shelter 开始表示保护。

items.en: Shelter named a building of refuge.
items.cn: shelter 指提供庇护的建筑。

items.en: The verb meant to protect or to hide.
items.cn: 动词形式意为保护或躲避。

note.en: Shelter is compared with similar-looking words and with words for refuge.
note.cn: 把 shelter 与形近词以及表示庇护的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Shelter is a shield for people and things, as a place, an act, or a state.
normalIntro.cn: shelter 是为人与物提供的盾，可以是地点、动作或状态。

normal.en: We took shelter from the rain.
The tree shelters the house from wind.
They built a shelter for the night.
normal.cn: 他们搭了个过夜的棚子。

normal.en: The animal shelter needs volunteers.
normal.cn: 动物收容所需要志愿者。

normal.en: The old shed sheltered the tools.

abstract.en: A shelter changes the weather without stopping it.
abstract.cn: 避难所改变天气的影响，却不阻止天气。

abstract.en: Protection is often a small roof and a thick wall.
abstract.cn: 保护常常只是小屋顶和厚墙。

abstract.en: To shelter another is to lend them your walls.
abstract.cn: 庇护他人就是把你的墙借给他们。

examples.en: They sheltered under a large tree.
examples.cn: 他们在一棵大树下避雨。

examples.en: The wall shelters the garden from wind.
They found shelter from the storm.
examples.cn: 他们找到了躲避暴风雨的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: shelter 源自中古英语 sheltron（盾牌方阵），核心义「盾一样的遮挡」，由军队护盾引申为避难所与保护。

root: 源自中古英语 sheltron（盾牌队伍），核心义「提供遮挡的盾」。

sensesIntro.en: Shelter means a protective place, to protect, to take cover, or the state of safety.
sensesIntro.cn: shelter 意为避难所、保护、躲避或受庇护状态。

core.en: A shield between a person and harm.
core.cn: 人与伤害之间的盾。

branches.en: A place that blocks weather.
To stand between harm and another.
To move under cover.
The state of being safe.
The place and the act share one word.
branches.cn: 地点与动作共用一个词。

intro.en: Shelter builds words for protection, its absence, and planted barriers.
intro.cn: shelter 构成表示保护、保护缺失和植物屏障的词。

latinIntro.en: Shelter has no Latin ancestor; Latin protectio, protection, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shelter 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 protectio（保护）只是语义对应词。

items.example: They live in a sheltered valley.
items.exampleCN: 他们住在避风的山谷里。

items.example: The sheltering trees blocked the wind.
The shelterer took in the family.

items.meaning: a line of trees for protection
trees left to protect new growth

definition_en: a broad piece of armour held for defence, something that protects, or to protect someone or something
core_image: 骑士举起一面宽大的木盾挡在身前
scene: 骑士举起了他的盾牌。The knight raised his shield.
sceneCN: 这里 shield 是「盾牌」（第 1 个义项）；句意：骑士举起了他的盾牌。

senses.title: Defensive board
senses.definition: a wide piece of metal or wood carried to stop blows
senses.definitionCN: 用来挡住击打的宽大金属板或木板
senses.example: The soldier hid behind his shield.
senses.why: This is the oldest and most concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老也最具体的义项。

senses.title: Protection
senses.definition: a person or thing that gives protection
senses.definitionCN: 提供保护的人或事物
senses.example: A tax shield saved the company money.
senses.exampleCN: 一项税收保护让公司省了钱。
senses.why: The board becomes any kind of barrier.
senses.whyCN: 盾牌引申为任何一种屏障。

senses.title: To protect
senses.definition: to protect someone or something from harm
senses.definitionCN: 保护某人或某物免受伤害
senses.example: Parents shield children from danger.
senses.exampleCN: 父母保护孩子远离危险。
senses.why: The noun turns into an action.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动作。

senses.title: To block
senses.definition: to hold something in front to stop light or view
senses.definitionCN: 把某物挡在前面以遮住光或视线
senses.example: She shielded her eyes from the sun.
senses.why: Protection narrows to blocking sight.
senses.whyCN: 保护义缩小为遮挡视线。

intro.en: Shield comes from an Old English word for a broad board carried in battle.
intro.cn: shield 来自古英语中表示战场上携带的宽板。

items.en: Scield meant a broad board carried for defence.
items.cn: scield 指战斗中携带的宽大防御板。

items.en: Skjoldr had the same shape and meaning.
items.cn: skjoldr 形状与含义都相同。

items.en: Sheld named both a guard in battle and a heraldic field.
items.cn: sheld 既指战阵中的护具，也指纹章上的盾形。

items.en: Shield extended to police barriers and protective covers.
items.cn: shield 扩展到防暴屏障与防护罩。

items.en: Shield became a verb meaning to protect.
items.cn: shield 成为表示保护的动词。

note.en: Shield is compared with similar-looking words and with words for protection.
note.cn: 把 shield 与形近词以及表示保护的词作比较。

entries.definition: a flat board for holding things
to keep someone safe from harm
to fight to keep something safe

normalIntro.en: A shield is a wall you carry: it stands between you and the blow.
normalIntro.cn: shield 是一堵随身携带的墙：挡在人和击打之间。

normal.en: The knight raised his shield.
A shield blocks the blow.
Parents shield children from harm.
normal.cn: 父母保护孩子免受伤害。

normal.en: He shielded his eyes from the sun.
The police carried riot shields.

abstract.en: A shield is a wall you carry.
abstract.cn: 盾牌是一堵随身携带的墙。

abstract.en: Protection often stands between two people.
abstract.cn: 保护常常站在两个人之间。

abstract.en: To shield is to take the first hit.
abstract.cn: 保护就是先承受那一击。

examples.en: The knight raised his shield.
Parents shield children from danger.
examples.cn: 父母保护孩子远离危险。

examples.en: She shielded her eyes from the sun.

dict_mnemonic.text: shield 与古英语 scield 同源，核心画面是「挡在身前的宽板」。

root: 源自原始日耳曼语 skelduz，核心义「宽大的防护板」。

sensesIntro.en: Shield means a defensive board, a protection, to protect, or to block.
sensesIntro.cn: shield 意为盾牌、保护物、保护或遮挡。

core.en: A broad board held between you and harm.
core.cn: 挡在人与伤害之间的一块宽板。

branches.en: The board carried in battle.
Anything that stands as protection.
branches.cn: 任何起保护作用的屏障。

branches.en: The act of protecting someone.
A hand held up against light.
The object and the action share one word.
branches.cn: 物件与动作共用一个词。

intro.en: Shield forms a small family of protection words.
intro.cn: shield 形成一个表示保护的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Shield has no Latin ancestor; Latin scutum, a shield, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shield 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 scutum（盾牌）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The shield was made of oak.
The wall provides shielding from noise.
items.exampleCN: 这堵墙起到隔音屏蔽作用。

items.example: He acted as a shielder for the team.

items.exampleCN: 没有盾牌的士兵向前迈步。

items.example: The leaf is broad and shieldlike.

definition_en: to move or change, or a work period or a small change
core_image: 一群人交接班，工作位置从左移到右
scene: 她在医院上夜班。She works the night shift at the hospital.
sceneCN: 这里 shift 是「班次」（第 3 个义项）；句意：她在医院上夜班。

senses.title: To move
senses.definition: to move from one place or position to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个地方或位置移到另一个
senses.example: He shifted the box to the left.
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的物理义项。

senses.title: To change
senses.definition: to change direction, opinion, or focus
senses.definitionCN: 改变方向、观点或焦点
senses.example: Public opinion shifted quickly.
senses.why: Physical movement becomes abstract change.
senses.whyCN: 物理移动引申为抽象改变。

senses.title: Work period
senses.definition: a period of work in a factory or hospital
senses.definitionCN: 工厂或医院里的一段工作时间
senses.example: She works the night shift at the hospital.
senses.why: Workers take turns, so time is divided.
senses.whyCN: 工人轮换，时间因此被划分。

senses.title: Small change
senses.definition: a small but important change
senses.definitionCN: 微小但重要的变化
senses.example: There was a shift in the wind.
senses.why: The noun names the result of shifting.
senses.whyCN: 名词指转移带来的结果。

intro.en: Shift began as a word for arranging and dividing things.
intro.cn: shift 最初表示安排和分配事物。

items.en: Sciftan meant to arrange or divide.
items.cn: sciftan 意为安排或划分。

items.en: Skipta meant to exchange or share out.
items.cn: skipta 意为交换或分配。

items.en: Shiften covered changing position or clothes.
items.cn: shiften 涵盖换位置或换衣服。

items.en: Shift named a period of work.
items.cn: shift 开始指一段工作时间。

items.en: Shift grew into a noun for a small change.
items.cn: shift 发展为表示微小变化的名词。

note.en: Shift is compared with similar-looking words and with words for change and movement.
note.cn: 把 shift 与形近词以及表示改变和移动的词作比较。

entries.definition: a piece of clothing for the upper body
a long narrow passage or rod
to exchange one thing for another

normalIntro.en: Shift is any move that changes place, time, or focus.
normalIntro.cn: shift 是改变位置、时间或焦点的任何移动。

normal.en: He shifted the box.
The wind shifted.
She works the night shift.
They shift gears on the hill.
The company shifted its focus.

abstract.en: A shift is a small move that changes everything.
abstract.cn: 转变是一个改变一切的小移动。

abstract.en: Night and day are two shifts of the same clock.
abstract.cn: 昼夜是同一座钟的两个班次。

abstract.en: To shift blame is to move a weight you should carry.
abstract.cn: 推卸责任就是搬走本该自己承担的重量。

examples.en: He shifted the box to the left.
She works the night shift at the hospital.
There was a shift in the wind.

dict_mnemonic.text: shift 的核心画面是「换位」：换位置、换时间、换重点，都叫 shift。

root: 源自古英语 sciftan（安排、划分），核心义「分开并重新分配」。

sensesIntro.en: Shift means to move, to change, a work period, or a small change.
sensesIntro.cn: shift 意为转移、改变、班次或转变。

core.en: Dividing and moving things to new places.
core.cn: 把事物分开并移到新位置。

branches.en: A box moved to another spot.
Opinion turns a new way.
A group takes its turn at work.
A small change in the wind.
Movement of things and change of views share one word.
branches.cn: 事物的移动与观点的变化共用一个词。

intro.en: Shift forms a family of movement and work words.
intro.cn: shift 形成一个表示移动和工作的词族。

latinIntro.en: Shift has no Latin ancestor; Latin mutare, to change, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shift 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 mutare（改变）只是语义对应词。

items.example: We need to shift the table.
She works two shifts a day.
The load shifted during the trip.
The shifting sand made walking hard.
items.exampleCN: 流动的沙子让行走变得困难。

items.meaning: a lever or person that shifts

items.example: He was called shiftless and lazy.

definition_en: the act of sending goods, or the goods that are sent together
core_image: 码头吊机把一只只货箱吊上船
scene: 港口堆场里，工人把打好的托盘装上卡车，准备发往海外客户。The forwarder confirmed that the shipment would leave the warehouse on Friday.
sceneCN: 这里 shipment 是「一批货物」（第 2 个义项：一次发运出去的那批货）；句意：货运代理确认这批货会在周五离开仓库。

derivatives.zh: ship 加施事后缀 -er，指「托运人；发货人」
ship 加 -ing 构成的名词，义为「运输；航运」
前缀 re- 加 shipment，义为「转运；再装运」

senses.title: The act of sending goods
senses.definition: the act of sending goods to a buyer, usually by ship, truck, train, or plane
senses.definitionCN: 把货物交给承运方运送给买方的动作
senses.example: The export team handles the shipment of every order.
senses.exampleCN: 出口团队负责每一张订单的装运。
senses.why: The suffix -ment names an action, so shipment first means the act of shipping.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把动作名词化，所以 shipment 首先指装运这个动作。

senses.title: A batch of goods sent
senses.definition: the goods that are sent together in one load
senses.definitionCN: 作为一批一起发运出去的货物
senses.example: The shipment arrived at the port two days late.
senses.exampleCN: 这批货晚了两天才到港口。
senses.why: From the action the word slides to its result: what is shipped is also called a shipment.
senses.whyCN: 从动作滑向结果：被装运出去的那批东西也叫 shipment。

senses.title: The loading of a vessel
senses.definition: the old sense of putting cargo onto a ship
senses.definitionCN: 把货物装上船这一较早的具体含义
senses.example: The old records list the shipment of coal at the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 旧档案里记载着在港口装运煤炭的事。
senses.why: The word began with ships, so loading a vessel is the oldest concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从船开始，所以把货装上船是最早的具体义项。

senses.title: A dispatch under a contract
senses.definition: one consignment among several that a contract allows to be sent separately
senses.definitionCN: 合同允许分开装运的若干批货中的一批
senses.example: The contract permits partial shipment in three lots.
senses.why: Trade contracts split a single order into shipments, so the word comes to mean one agreed dispatch.
senses.whyCN: 贸易合同把一张订单拆成若干次装运，于是 shipment 也指约定好的一次发货。

senses.title: Freight transport as a whole
senses.definition: the business or volume of carrying goods, especially by sea
senses.definitionCN: 承运货物的行业或运量，尤指海运
senses.example: The town economy depends on shipment and storage.
senses.exampleCN: 这个城镇的经济依靠货运与仓储。
senses.why: The action sense broadens from one dispatch to the whole traffic of goods.
senses.whyCN: 动作义再从一次发货扩大到整个货运行业与运量。

intro.en: Shipment is ship plus the noun suffix -ment, which English received through French from Latin -mentum; it first names the loading of a ship and then the goods sent and the act of sending them.
intro.cn: shipment 由 ship 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，而 -ment 是英语经法语从拉丁语 -mentum 借来的；它最初指装船，后来兼指发出的货物与发运这个动作。

items.en: -mentum is a Latin noun suffix that forms nouns of action or result.
items.cn: 拉丁语后缀 -mentum 由动词构成表示动作或结果的名词。

items.en: -ment reaches English through Old French, where it marks nouns of action.
items.cn: -ment 经古法语进入英语，在法语里就用来标记动作名词。

items.en: Ship, from Old English scip, joins -ment to name the loading of a vessel.
items.cn: 来自古英语 scip 的 ship 与 -ment 结合，指把货装上船。

items.en: Shipment widens from loading a ship to sending goods by any carrier.
items.cn: shipment 从装船扩大到用任何承运方式发货。

items.en: Trade papers later speak of the goods themselves as a shipment, and of partial shipment.
items.cn: 后来的贸易文书把发出的货物本身也叫 shipment，并有了分批装运的说法。

note.en: Shipment is ship plus -ment, so it stands beside ship, shipper, and shipping, and near consignment, cargo, and delivery.
note.cn: shipment 由 ship 加 -ment 构成，因此与 ship、shipper、shipping 相邻，并与 consignment、cargo、delivery 意义相近。

entries.definition: to send goods, or a large boat
entries.definitionCN: 运送货物，或指大船，是 shipment 的基础词

entries.definition: the person or firm that sends goods
entries.definitionCN: 托运人；发货人，由 ship 加 -er 构成

entries.definition: the transport of goods, especially by sea
entries.definitionCN: 运输；航运，由 ship 加 -ing 构成

entries.definition: a batch of goods sent to a buyer or an agent
entries.definitionCN: 托运的一批货，强调按委托发出

entries.definition: the goods carried by a ship, plane, or truck
entries.definitionCN: 货物，强调运输工具上装载的东西

entries.definition: the act of bringing goods to the buyer
entries.definitionCN: 交付；送货，强调送到买方手上

normalIntro.en: Shipment is ship plus -ment, and the suffix turns the act of shipping into a noun that also names the goods shipped.
normalIntro.cn: shipment 是 ship 加 -ment，后缀把装运这个动作变成名词，同时也指被运走的货物。

normal.en: Shipment is ship plus -ment: the suffix turns the act of shipping into a noun.
normal.cn: shipment 由 ship 加 -ment 构成，后缀把装运动作变成名词。

normal.en: Old English scip is the word for ship, so shipment began with cargo on water.
normal.cn: 古英语 scip 就是船，所以 shipment 最早指水上的货运。

normal.en: A shipment date is the day the goods must leave, not the day they arrive.
normal.cn: shipment date 是货物必须发出的日子，不是到达的日子。

normal.en: Partial shipment means the order goes out in several separate loads.
normal.cn: partial shipment 指订单分成几次装运发出。

normal.en: Compare cargo: cargo is what a vehicle carries, while a shipment is a batch sent under one order.
normal.cn: 对比 cargo：cargo 是运输工具上装的东西，shipment 是按一张订单发出的一批货。

abstract.en: Picture a crane lifting a steel container onto a deck.
abstract.cn: 想象吊机把一只钢制集装箱吊上甲板。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed pallet with a shipping label on the corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一只封好的托盘，角上贴着货运标签。

abstract.en: Picture a ship whose decks are stacked with boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘船，甲板上堆满货箱。

examples.en: The first shipment left the factory on Monday.
examples.cn: 第一批货在周一离开了工厂。

examples.en: A shipment of spare parts is waiting at customs.
examples.cn: 一批备件正在海关等待放行。

examples.en: The contract allows two shipments in partial lots.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喜普门」——货箱进了这扇门，就被装运走了；谐音联想，不是词源。

sensesIntro.en: Shipment starts from the act of loading and sending goods, then names the goods sent, the older loading of a vessel, one contracted dispatch, and freight traffic as a whole.
sensesIntro.cn: shipment 从装货发运这个动作出发，进而指发出的货物、较早的装船义、合同下的一次发货，以及整体的货运。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crane lifting boxes onto a ship at the quay.

intro.en: Shipment is the Old English noun ship plus the noun suffix -ment, which English took from Latin -mentum through French.

latinIntro.en: Latin -mentum turns verbs into nouns of action or result, and French -ment carried that job into English.

definition_en: to fire a weapon, send something out quickly, film something, score in basketball, or a new plant growth

senses.title: Fire a weapon

senses.why: This is the basic violent sense.

senses.title: Send out quickly

senses.title: Film
senses.definition: to record a film or photograph

senses.title: Score a basket

senses.title: New growth

abstract.en: A show is a secret given light.

abstract.en: To show is to lend your eyes to another.
abstract.cn: 展示就是把你的眼睛借给别人。

abstract.en: Proof is a fact put on stage.

examples.en: She showed the photo to everyone.

definition_zh: 淋浴；阵雨；送礼聚会；大量给予
definition_en: a wash under falling water, a short fall of rain, a party for giving gifts, or to give many things
core_image: 花洒喷出细密水线，热气在浴室里升起
scene: 他每天早上冲个淋浴。He takes a shower every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 shower 是「淋浴」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他每天早上冲个淋浴。

senses.title: A wash
senses.definition: a wash under a spray of falling water
senses.definitionCN: 在落下的水流下洗澡
senses.example: He takes a shower every morning.
senses.why: This is the everyday bathroom sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常浴室场景中的义项。

senses.title: A rain
senses.definition: a short fall of rain
senses.definitionCN: 短时间的一阵降雨
senses.example: A shower passed over the town.
senses.why: Falling water connects rain and washing.
senses.whyCN: 落下的水流把雨和淋浴联系起来。

senses.title: A gift party
senses.definition: a party where gifts are given, especially for a baby or a bride
senses.definitionCN: 赠送礼物的聚会，尤指为婴儿或新娘举办
senses.example: They held a baby shower for her.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为她办了一场迎婴聚会。
senses.why: Gifts fall on the guest like rain.
senses.whyCN: 礼物像雨一样落在客人身上。

senses.title: To give much
senses.definition: to give someone many things or much attention
senses.definitionCN: 给某人许多东西或大量关注
senses.example: Fans showered her with flowers.
senses.why: The rain image turns into an abundance of gifts.
senses.whyCN: 雨的意象转化为礼物的丰盛。

intro.en: Shower first meant a brief fall of rain.

items.en: Scur meant a brief storm or shower.

items.en: Shour named a fall of rain.

items.en: The washing sense appeared with indoor plumbing.
items.cn: 随着室内管道出现，淋浴义项产生了。

items.en: A party for giving gifts took the name.

items.en: The verb came to mean to give in large amounts.
items.cn: 动词义发展为大量给予。

note.cn: 把 shower 与形近词以及表示洗浴和降雨的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: A shower is rain invited indoors, or gifts falling like rain.
normalIntro.cn: shower 是被请进室内的雨，或像雨一样落下的礼物。

normal.en: He takes a shower every morning.
A shower passed over the town.
They held a baby shower for her.

The showerhead is broken.

abstract.en: A shower is rain that agrees to stay in one room.
abstract.cn: 淋浴是愿意留在一个房间里的雨。

abstract.en: Gifts can fall as softly as warm rain.
abstract.cn: 礼物可以像暖雨一样轻轻落下。

abstract.en: Kindness often arrives in showers, not drops.

examples.en: He takes a shower every morning.

dict_mnemonic.text: shower 本来是「一阵雨」：水从上往下落，落在身上是淋浴，落在礼物上就是大量赠送。

root: 源自古英语 scur（短暂风雨、阵雨），核心义「从上方落下的一阵水或物」。

Friends gather to give gifts.

definition_en: to become smaller, to become smaller after washing, to move back in fear, or to decrease
core_image: 一件毛衣在热水里越缩越小，袖口慢慢收紧
scene: 羊毛衫洗后缩水了。The wool sweater shrank in the wash.
sceneCN: 这里 shrink 是「缩小」（第 1 个义项）；句意：羊毛衫洗后缩水了。

senses.title: To become smaller
senses.definition: to become smaller in size or amount
senses.definitionCN: 尺寸或数量变小
senses.example: The sweater shrank in the wash.
senses.why: This is the central physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的物理义项。

senses.title: Cloth shrinking
senses.definition: to become smaller after being washed
senses.definitionCN: 洗涤后变小
senses.example: Hot water can shrink wool.
senses.why: Cloth is the most familiar victim of shrinking.
senses.whyCN: 布料是最常见的缩水对象。

senses.title: To move back
senses.definition: to move back because of fear or dislike
senses.definitionCN: 因害怕或厌恶而后退
senses.example: The child shrank from the dog.
senses.why: The body makes itself smaller when afraid.
senses.whyCN: 害怕时身体会把自己缩小。

senses.title: To decrease
senses.definition: to become fewer or less
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度变少
senses.example: Profits shrank last year.
senses.why: Numbers shrink as well as cloth.
senses.whyCN: 数字和布料一样会缩小。

items.en: Slang called a psychiatrist a shrink.
items.cn: 俚语用 shrink 称呼精神科医生。

note.en: Shrink is compared with similar-looking words and with words for becoming less.
note.cn: 把 shrink 与形近词以及表示变小的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Shrink means pulling inward, whether in cloth, numbers, or courage.
normalIntro.cn: shrink 是向内收拢，无论收的是布料、数字还是勇气。

normal.en: The sweater shrank in the wash.
Hot water can shrink wool.

abstract.en: Cloth remembers heat by becoming smaller.
abstract.cn: 布料用变小来记住热度。

abstract.en: Fear makes the body shrink before the mind agrees.

abstract.en: A shrinking market is a quiet warning.
abstract.cn: 萎缩的市场是一个安静的警告。

examples.en: The sweater shrank in the wash.

Profits shrank last year.

root: 源自古英语 scrincan（枯萎、干缩），核心义「向内收拢、变小」。

intro.en: Shrink builds a family of size and protection words.

latinIntro.en: Shrink is Germanic; Latin contrahere, to draw together, is only a semantic parallel.

items.example: The gap will shrink over time.

definition_zh: 灌木；灌木丛；（园艺）花灌木；灌木层；果味糖浆饮（旧义，另源）
definition_en: a woody plant smaller than a tree, usually with several stems growing from the base
core_image: 一株不到腰高的木本植物，从同一个基部抽出三根细茎，旁边高树的树干已经枯死
scene: 同一基部抽出三根细茎的矮灌木，在高树枯死的地方仍然活着。A low shrub with three stems from the same base survived where the taller trees had died.
sceneCN: 这里 shrub 指「低于乔木、通常自基部分出多根茎的木本植物」（第 1 个义项：小型多茎木本植物）；句意为同一基部抽出三根茎的矮灌木，在高树枯死之处存活下来。图中可辨识物件：三根细茎、共同基部、枯死的高树干、裸露地面。

pos.zh: 灌木；灌木丛（可数；集合义不可数）
果味糖浆饮（加醋或酒，18 世纪旧义，词源不同）

forms.label: 形容词（灌木状的；多灌木的）
名词（灌木丛；灌木栽植区）

derivatives.zh: 半灌木（基部木质、上部草质）

senses.title: A small multi-stemmed woody plant
senses.definition: a woody plant that stays low and usually sends up several stems from the same base instead of one trunk
senses.definitionCN: 一种低矮的木本植物，通常自同一基部长出多根茎，而非单一下干
senses.example: A low shrub with three stems from the same base survived the drought.
senses.exampleCN: 同一基部抽出三根茎的矮灌木熬过了干旱。
senses.why: the word's core is lowness plus woodiness: it is not a small tree because it branches at the ground.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是「低矮」加「木质」：它不是小树，因为它在贴地处就分叉。

senses.title: Shrubs planted as a garden mass
senses.titleCN: 庭园中成片栽植的灌木
senses.definition: a group or mass of low woody plants grown together for cover, flowers or boundary
senses.definitionCN: 成片栽植的低矮木本植物，用于遮蔽、观花或作边界
senses.example: The gardener cut the shrub back hard after flowering.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁在花后把这丛灌木重剪了一遍。
senses.why: in garden talk the countable plant and the uncountable mass blur, so 'the shrub' can mean the whole bed.
senses.whyCN: 在园艺口语中，单株与成片混在一起，因此这个说法也可指整片花坛。

senses.title: The botanical growth form
senses.titleCN: 植物学上的灌木生长型
senses.definition: a growth form defined by persistent woody stems branching near ground level and a mature height well below the tree layer
senses.definitionCN: 一种生长型：具宿存木质茎、贴近地面分枝，成熟高度远低于乔木层
senses.example: The flora keys out the shrub by its basal branching, not by its height alone.
senses.exampleCN: 这本植物志以基部分枝、而非单以高度来检索灌木。
senses.why: botany needs a form category between herb and tree, and shrub names exactly that middle.
senses.whyCN: 植物学需要一个介于草本与乔木之间的形态类别，shrub 正指这个中间层。

senses.title: A flowering ornamental shrub
senses.definition: a woody plant chosen and pruned mainly for showy flowers or coloured foliage in a garden
senses.definitionCN: 主要因花艳或叶色而在庭园中被选用、修剪的木本植物
senses.example: A pink flowering shrub anchors the corner of the border.
senses.exampleCN: 一株开粉花的灌木压住花坛转角。
senses.why: horticulture shifted the emphasis from wild form to cultivated display, so shrub came to mean a planted ornament.
senses.whyCN: 园艺学把重点从野生形态移到栽培展示，于是 shrub 也指栽下的观赏植物。

senses.title: The shrub layer of a forest
senses.definition: the vertical layer of woody plants between the herb layer and the tree canopy
senses.definitionCN: 位于草本层与乔木树冠之间的木本植物层
senses.example: Deer browsing has stripped the shrub layer from the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 鹿的啃食已把这片林子的灌木层剥光。
senses.why: in ecology a single plant gives its name to a whole stratum, because that layer is made of such plants.
senses.whyCN: 生态学中用单株植物之名指整个层，因为该层正是由这类植物构成。

senses.title: A dryland or scrub shrub
senses.definition: a tough, often thorny or waxy-leaved woody plant that dominates dry scrub and semi-desert
senses.definitionCN: 常带刺或具蜡质叶的耐旱木本植物，在干旱灌丛与半荒漠中占优势
senses.example: Salt-tolerant shrubs line the dry lake bed.
senses.exampleCN: 耐盐灌木沿干涸湖床排成一线。
senses.why: where trees cannot hold, shrubs become the dominant cover, so the word doubles as a landscape label.
senses.whyCN: 在乔木立不住的地方，灌木成为主要覆盖，于是这个词也兼作景观标签。

senses.title: Woody encroachment on open land
senses.definition: the spread of woody plants into grassland or pasture, often seen as degradation
senses.definitionCN: 木本植物向草地或牧场扩张，常被视为退化
senses.example: Unchecked grazing let shrub take over the lower pasture.
senses.exampleCN: 放牧失控让灌木占据了低处牧场。
senses.why: a plant name turns into a process name when the plant's spread changes what the land is.
senses.whyCN: 当某种植物的扩张改变了土地性质，植物名就变成了过程名。

senses.title: The old fruit-syrup drink
senses.titleCN: 旧时的果味糖浆饮（另源）
senses.definition: a drink made from fruit juice, sugar and vinegar or rum, popular in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries
senses.definitionCN: 由果汁、糖与醋或朗姆酒调成的饮品，在 18 至 19 世纪流行
senses.example: A jug of raspberry shrub stood cooling on the sill.
senses.exampleCN: 一罐覆盆子糖浆饮放在窗台上晾凉。
senses.why: this is a homonym, not a development of the plant sense: it comes through Arabic sharab 'a drink'.
senses.whyCN: 这是同形异源词，并非植物义的引申：它经阿拉伯语 sharab「饮料」而来。

intro.en: Shrub 'low woody plant' is a Germanic word of uncertain deeper origin; shrub 'fruit drink' is an unrelated homonym from Arabic.
intro.cn: shrub「低矮木本植物」是日耳曼词，更深来源不确定；shrub「果汁饮」则是来自阿拉伯语的不相关同形词。

items.en: Old English scrybb named brushwood and low woody growth. The form is recorded chiefly in glosses, so its early history is thin.
items.cn: 古英语 scrybb 指柴枝与低矮木本植物。该形式主要见于注释文献，早期历史材料很少。

items.en: The word matches North Frisian skrobb 'brushwood' and West Flemish schrobbe 'climbing vetch', which points to a North Sea Germanic stock.
items.cn: 这个词与北弗里斯兰语 skrobb「柴枝」、西佛兰德语 schrobbe「野豌豆」相合，指向北海日耳曼语来源。

items.en: Middle English shrub kept both the plant and the cut-brushwood readings, and the plant sense gradually dominated.
items.cn: 中古英语 shrub 同时保留「植物」与「砍下的柴枝」两义，后来植物义逐渐占主导。

items.en: The drink shrub entered English in the eighteenth century through Arabic sharab 'a drink' (compare sherbet and syrup), a completely separate line.
items.cn: 指饮品的 shrub 于 18 世纪经阿拉伯语 sharab「饮料」进入英语（参较 sherbet 与 syrup），是完全独立的一线。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first date): no Germanic etymon beyond the North Sea forms is attested, and the pre-Germanic root is a reconstruction; the first English citation of the plant sense is not securely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：除北海诸语形式外没有更早的日耳曼语书证，其日耳曼语之前的词根属重构；植物义的最早英语书证年代也不可靠。

note.en: Group one separates shrub from its closest woody-plant neighbours; group two separates the vegetation words that are not single plants.
note.cn: 第一组把 shrub 与最接近的木本植物词分开；第二组区分那些指植被而非单株的词。

entries.definition: A general word for a low woody plant, often wild and rounded; shrub is the more technical and garden term.
entries.definitionCN: 低矮木本植物的通称，常指野生、团状者；shrub 更技术化，也更常用于园艺。

entries.definition: Low woody vegetation as a cover type, often stunted or thorny; it rarely names a single plant.
entries.definitionCN: 作为覆盖类型的低矮木本植被，常矮小或多刺；很少指单株植物。

entries.definition: A young tree with a single stem; it differs from a shrub in having one trunk that will grow tall.
entries.definitionCN: 单茎的幼树；与灌木的区别在于只有一根将来会长高的主干。

entries.definition: A plant woody only at the base and herbaceous above, so it dies back partly each winter.
entries.definitionCN: 仅基部木质、上部草质的植物，每年冬季部分枯死。

entries.definition: A planted area of shrubs, usually in a garden or park; it names the bed, not the species.
entries.definitionCN: 庭园或公园中成片栽植的灌木区；指花坛，不指物种。

entries.definition: The low plants growing beneath a forest canopy, including herbs and shrubs; broader than shrub.
entries.definitionCN: 林冠下生长的低矮植物，含草本与灌木；范围比 shrub 宽。

entries.definition: A line of shrubs planted and clipped as a barrier; the shrubs are means, the barrier is the point.
entries.definitionCN: 成行栽植并修剪作屏障的灌木；灌木是手段，屏障才是目的。

entries.definition: A dense stand of shrubs or small trees hard to walk through; it stresses impenetrability.
entries.definitionCN: 难以穿行的密集灌木或小树丛；强调难以通过。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: One base, many stems: that is the difference between a shrub and a tree.
normal.cn: 一个基部、多根茎：这就是灌木与乔木的区别。

normal.en: The family runs shrub, shrubby, shrubbery, shrubland, subshrub.
Fixed phrases: flowering shrub, evergreen shrub, shrub layer, desert shrub.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：花灌木、常绿灌木、灌木层、荒漠灌木。

normal.en: Ecology names a whole layer after the plant: the shrub layer.
normal.cn: 生态学以这种植物之名为整层命名：灌木层。

normal.en: The homonym warning: the fruit drink comes from Arabic, not from the plant.
normal.cn: 同形异源提醒：果汁饮来自阿拉伯语，与植物无关。

abstract.en: Think of a hand that never grew one wrist but five fingers straight from the palm.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手没有手腕，五根手指直接从掌心长出。

abstract.en: Think of a low wall that keeps growing back after every cut.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵矮墙，每次被砍后都重新长回。

abstract.en: Think of a crowd of short people holding a tall forest up from below.
abstract.cn: 想象一群矮个子在下面把高处的森林托住。

examples.en: Goats will eat almost any shrub before they touch the grass.
examples.cn: 山羊几乎先吃光任何灌木，才去碰草。

examples.en: The shrub layer recovered two years after the fire.
examples.cn: 火灾两年后灌木层恢复了。

examples.en: A single shrub can anchor a whole dune.
examples.cn: 一株灌木就能固定整座沙丘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「shrub」读音像「刷布」——矮矮一丛，像刷子一样贴地散开 → 灌木

root: 古英语 scrybb「柴枝、低矮木本植物」，与北弗里斯兰语 skrobb、西佛兰德语 schrobbe 同源，属北海日耳曼语一线；更深词根不确定。指饮品的 shrub 另出阿拉伯语 sharab。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one plant: it grows low and many-stemmed, fills gardens and forest layers, takes over dry ground, and finally shares its spelling with an unrelated drink.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一株植物展开：它低矮多茎，填满庭园与森林层次，占据干旱地，最后又与一种无关的饮料共用拼写。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one root crown sending up several thin stems instead of a single trunk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个根颈抽出几根细茎，而不是一根主干。

branches.en: FORM: lowness and basal branching define the plant both in common speech and in botany.
branches.cn: 形态：低矮与基部分枝，在日常语与植物学中都定义这种植物。

branches.en: GARDEN: the plant becomes an ornamental mass chosen for flower and boundary.
branches.cn: 庭园：这种植物成为按花与边界选用的观赏群体。

branches.en: STRATUM: in a wood the same plant gives its name to a whole layer.
branches.cn: 层次：在林中，同一种植物为整个层命名。

branches.en: DRY LAND: where trees fail, shrubs dominate, and their spread can count as degradation.
branches.cn: 旱地：乔木立不住时灌木占优，其扩张可算作退化。

branches.en: HOMONYM: the drink is a separate Arabic loan, so the two meanings must not be linked.
branches.cn: 同形异源：饮料是独立的阿拉伯语借词，两义不可串联。

intro.en: Shrub is a free root that takes several suffixes, producing a compact family of plant and landscape words.
intro.cn: shrub 是自由词根，可接若干后缀，形成一组紧凑的植物与景观词族。

latinIntro.en: Shrub has no Latin ancestor; the only Latin-looking item here, sub-, is a prefix borrowed into English word formation, not evidence of a Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: shrub 没有拉丁语祖先；此处唯一像拉丁语的 sub- 是英语构词借用的前缀，不能当作拉丁词根的证据。

items.example: The shrub regrew from the cut stems.
items.exampleCN: 这株灌木从被砍的茎上重新长出。

items.meaning: like a shrub; full of shrubs
items.example: The shrubby slope holds the soil.
items.exampleCN: 长满灌木的坡地能保住土壤。

items.example: A clipped shrubbery hides the wall.
items.exampleCN: 一片修剪过的灌木丛遮住了墙。
灌木林地取代了过牧的牧场。

items.meaning: a plant woody only at the base
items.example: Lavender is often grown as a subshrub.
items.exampleCN: 薰衣草常被当作半灌木栽培。

items.example: The sprayed verge was almost shrubless.
items.exampleCN: 喷过药的路边几乎没有灌木。

items.meaning: where shrubs are the main cover
items.example: A shrub-dominated community followed the fire.
items.exampleCN: 火灾后形成以灌木为主的群落。
灌木草原上长着山艾与丛生禾草。

definition_zh: 耸肩；表示怀疑；不理会；耸肩动作
definition_en: to raise the shoulders to show doubt or indifference, to dismiss something, or such a movement
core_image: 一个人双肩一抬，嘴角一撇，表示自己也不知道
scene: 他耸耸肩说不知道。He shrugged and said he did not know.
sceneCN: 这里 shrug 是「耸肩」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他耸耸肩说不知道。

senses.title: To raise the shoulders
senses.definition: to raise the shoulders slightly
senses.definitionCN: 轻轻抬起双肩
senses.example: He shrugged and said he did not know.
senses.why: This is the basic gesture.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的手势义项。

senses.title: To show doubt
senses.definition: to use the gesture to show doubt
senses.definitionCN: 用这个动作表示怀疑
senses.example: She shrugged at my question.
senses.exampleCN: 她对我的问题耸了耸肩。
senses.why: The movement answers a question without words.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作不用语言就回答了问题。

senses.title: To dismiss
senses.definition: to treat something as unimportant
senses.definitionCN: 把某事当作不重要
senses.example: He shrugged off the criticism.
senses.why: The gesture can push a problem away.
senses.whyCN: 这个手势可以把问题推开。

senses.title: The movement
senses.definition: the act of raising the shoulders
senses.definitionCN: 抬起肩膀的动作
senses.example: She answered with a shrug.
senses.why: The verb turns into a noun for the gesture.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为表示该手势的名词。

intro.en: Shrug is a Middle English word whose deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: shrug 是中东英语词，更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Shruggen meant to raise the shoulders.
items.cn: shruggen 意为抬起肩膀。

items.en: The word may echo the movement itself.
items.cn: 这个词可能模仿动作本身。

items.en: The gesture became a sign of doubt.
items.cn: 这个手势成为怀疑的标志。

items.en: Shrug off came to mean to dismiss.
items.cn: shrug off 逐渐表示不理会。

items.en: The noun named the movement itself.
items.cn: 名词指动作本身。

note.en: Shrug is compared with similar-looking words and with words for gestures and dismissal.
note.cn: 把 shrug 与形近词以及表示手势和不予理会的词作比较。

entries.definition: to move the head up and down
to decide something is not important

normalIntro.en: A shrug is a sentence spoken with the shoulders.
normalIntro.cn: 耸肩是用肩膀说出的一句话。

normal.en: He shrugged and said he did not know.
She shrugged at my question.
normal.cn: 她对我的问题耸了耸肩。

normal.en: He shrugged off the criticism.
She answered with a shrug.
Do not shrug away your chance.

abstract.en: A shrug says what words are too tired to say.
abstract.cn: 耸肩说出了词语累得说不出口的话。

abstract.en: To shrug off a burden is to set it down.
abstract.cn: 甩开负担就是把它放下。

abstract.en: The smallest gesture can close a long argument.
abstract.cn: 最小的手势也能结束一场长争论。

examples.en: He shrugged and said he did not know.
She answered with a shrug.
He shrugged off the criticism.

dict_mnemonic.text: shrug 把两个肩膀往上一抬：抬起来表示不知道，抬完放下表示不在乎。

root: 源自中古英语 shruggen（抬肩），核心义「用肩部动作表达态度」。

sensesIntro.en: Shrug means to raise the shoulders, show doubt, dismiss something, or such a movement.
sensesIntro.cn: shrug 意为耸肩、表示怀疑、不理会或耸肩动作。

core.en: Shoulders rise to say what words will not.
core.cn: 双肩抬起，说出词语不愿说的话。

branches.en: The shoulders move upward.
The body admits it does not know.
The gesture pushes a problem away.
The movement becomes a noun.
Doubt and dismissal share the same small motion.
branches.cn: 怀疑与不理会共享同一个小动作。

intro.en: Shrug builds a small family of gesture words.
intro.cn: shrug 构成表示手势的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Shrug is Germanic; Latin gestus, a gesture, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shrug 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 gestus（手势）只是语义对应词。

items.example: She shrugs when she is unsure.
She stood shrugging at the door.

items.meaning: to push away with a shrug

definition_en: a sound, light, or action that carries a message, or a sign of something
core_image: 铁轨旁的红灯亮起，列车应声停下
scene: 火车鸣笛发出信号，缓缓启动。The train gave a signal and slowly started.
sceneCN: 这里 signal 是「信号」（第 1 个义项）；句意：火车发出信号，缓缓启动。

senses.title: A message sent by sound or light
senses.definition: a sound, light, or movement that sends a message
senses.definitionCN: 传递信息的声音、光或动作
senses.example: The train gave a signal and slowly started.
senses.exampleCN: 火车发出信号，缓缓启动。
senses.why: This is the basic message sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的信息义项。

senses.title: A traffic light
senses.definition: a set of lights that controls traffic
senses.definitionCN: 控制交通的一组灯
senses.example: Turn left at the next signal.
senses.exampleCN: 在下一个信号灯处左转。
senses.why: A light on the road is a public message.
senses.whyCN: 路上的灯是给公众的信息。

senses.title: A sign of something
senses.definition: something that shows a change or a likely event
senses.definitionCN: 表明变化或可能发生之事的现象
senses.example: The report is a signal of change.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是变化的信号。
senses.why: Any message can be read from events.
senses.whyCN: 任何信息都可以从事态中读出。

intro.en: Signal grew from the Latin word for a sign.
intro.cn: signal 由拉丁语中表示记号的词发展而来。

items.en: Signum meant a mark or sign.
items.cn: signum 意为记号或标志。

items.en: Signale meant a sign or signal.
items.cn: signale 意为标志或信号。

items.en: The word entered French as signal.
items.cn: 这个词以 signal 进入法语。

items.en: English used signal for messages by sound or light.
items.cn: 英语用 signal 表示声光传递的信息。

items.en: The word also named traffic lights.
items.cn: 这个词也用来指交通信号灯。

note.en: Signal is compared with similar-looking words and with message words.
note.cn: 把 signal 与形近词以及表示信息的词作比较。

entries.definition: a signal for someone to act
a sign that something is true

normalIntro.en: A signal is a message that travels through light or sound.
normalIntro.cn: signal 是借着光或声音传递的信息。

normal.en: The train gave a signal and slowly started.
normal.cn: 火车发出信号，缓缓启动。

normal.en: Turn left at the next signal.
normal.cn: 在下一个信号灯处左转。

normal.en: The phone signal was weak.
She raised her hand as a signal.
The report is a signal of change.
normal.cn: 这份报告是变化的信号。

abstract.en: A signal is a message in a hurry.
abstract.cn: 信号是匆忙上路的信息。

abstract.en: Light and sound can carry agreement.
abstract.cn: 光和声音也能承载约定。

abstract.en: Small signals prevent large accidents.
abstract.cn: 小小的信号防止大大的事故。

examples.en: The train gave a signal and slowly started.
examples.cn: 火车发出信号，缓缓启动。

examples.en: Turn left at the next signal.
examples.cn: 在下一个信号灯处左转。

examples.en: The report is a signal of change.
examples.cn: 这份报告是变化的信号。

dict_mnemonic.text: sign（记号）加 -al 变成 signal：一个记号还不够，要会发声发光的记号，就是信号。

root: 源自拉丁语 signum（记号），经中世纪拉丁语 signale 发展而来，核心义「传递信息的记号」。

sensesIntro.en: Signal means a message by sound or light, a traffic light, or a sign of change.
sensesIntro.cn: signal 意为声光信号、交通信号灯或变化的迹象。

core.en: A sign sent through the air.
core.cn: 经空气传送的记号。

branches.en: The whistle sends a signal.
The traffic signal turns red.
The report signals change.
Both are messages for many people.
branches.cn: 两者都是给许多人的信息。

branches.en: A light and a hint both guide.

intro.en: Signal builds a family of message and traffic words.
intro.cn: signal 构成表示信息与交通的词族。

latinIntro.en: Signal comes through French from Latin signum, a mark.
latinIntro.cn: signal 经由法语来自拉丁语 signum（记号）。

items.meaning: a message by sound or light

items.example: The signals were hard to see.
The signaller waved the train on.
items.exampleCN: 信号员挥手让火车前进。

items.meaning: a railway worker who works signals

items.example: The signal tower stood on the hill.

definition_en: a person's written name, the act of signing, or a distinctive feature
core_image: 笔尖在合同末尾划出熟悉的一串字
scene: 请在表格底部签上你的名字。Please put your signature at the bottom of the form.
sceneCN: 这里 signature 是「签名」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请在表格底部签名。

senses.title: A written name
senses.definition: a person's name written by that person
senses.definitionCN: 本人亲手写下的名字
senses.example: Please put your signature at the bottom of the form.
senses.why: This is the basic written-name sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的书写姓名义项。

senses.title: The act of signing
senses.definition: the act of writing one's name to agree or approve
senses.definitionCN: 写下名字表示同意或批准的行为
senses.example: The signature of the contract took place today.
senses.why: The written name also names the act.
senses.whyCN: 写下的名字也用来指这个行为。

senses.title: A distinctive feature
senses.definition: a feature that clearly identifies a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 能清楚表明某人或某物身份的特征
senses.example: That song is her signature.
senses.why: A signature marks an identity, not only a name.
senses.whyCN: 签名标记身份，不只是名字。

intro.en: Signature comes from a Latin word for marking.
intro.cn: signature 来自表示做标记的拉丁语词。

items.en: Signum meant a mark or sign.
items.cn: signum 意为记号或标志。

items.en: Signatura meant a marking or a sign.
items.cn: signatura 意为标记或记号。

items.en: English borrowed it as signatur.
items.cn: 英语借入时写作 signatur。

items.en: The word settled as signature.
items.cn: 词形固定为 signature。

items.en: It also came to mean a distinctive feature.
items.cn: 它也逐渐表示鲜明特色。

note.en: Signature is compared with similar-looking words and with words for names.
note.cn: 把 signature 与形近词以及表示名字的词作比较。

entries.definition: a message by sound or light

normalIntro.en: A signature is a name that proves identity.
normalIntro.cn: 签名是证明身份的名字。

normal.en: Please put your signature at the bottom of the form.
They collected signatures for the petition.
The chef's signature dish is fish soup.
normal.cn: 这位厨师的招牌菜是鱼汤。

normal.en: The signature looked forged.
normal.cn: 这个签名看起来是伪造的。

normal.en: Her signature style is simple and bold.
normal.cn: 她的标志性风格简洁而大胆。

abstract.en: A signature is a promise written in ink.
abstract.cn: 签名是用墨水写下的承诺。

abstract.en: A name can become a personal mark.
abstract.cn: 名字可以变成个人的标记。

abstract.en: What we repeat becomes our signature.
abstract.cn: 我们反复做的事成了自己的标志。

examples.en: Please put your signature at the bottom of the form.
They collected signatures for the petition.
That song is her signature.

dict_mnemonic.text: sign（记号）加 -ature 变成 signature：写下的名字就是最个人的记号。

root: 源自中世纪拉丁语 signatura（标记），与 signum（记号）同源，核心义「个人标记」。

sensesIntro.en: Signature means a written name, the act of signing, or a distinctive feature.
sensesIntro.cn: signature 意为签名、签署行为或鲜明特色。

core.en: A personal mark made with a hand.
core.cn: 用手写下的个人标记。

branches.en: A name is written at the bottom.
The contract is signed today.
One dish carries the chef's mark.
branches.cn: 一道菜带着厨师的标记。

branches.en: The name and the act are linked.
The mark proves identity.

intro.en: Signature belongs to the sign family of marking words.
intro.cn: signature 属于 sign 这一标记词族。

latinIntro.en: Signature comes from Latin signum through Medieval Latin signatura.
latinIntro.cn: signature 由拉丁语 signum 经中世纪拉丁语 signatura 演变而来。

items.exampleCN: 签署仪式吸引了一群人。

items.meaning: a person who signs an agreement
items.exampleCN: 每位签署者都拿到一份副本。

items.meaning: a dish a restaurant is known for
items.example: The soup is their signature dish.
items.exampleCN: 这道汤是他们的招牌菜。

items.example: Bright colors are her signature style.
items.exampleCN: 鲜艳的色彩是她的标志性风格。

definition_en: the importance of something, or its meaning
core_image: 一枚小印章落在公文上，文件顿时有了分量
scene: 这一发现对医学有重大意义。The discovery is of great significance to medicine.
sceneCN: 这里 significance 是「意义」（第 2 个义项）；句意：这一发现对医学有重大意义。

senses.title: Importance
senses.definition: the quality of being important or worth attention
senses.definitionCN: 重要或值得关注的性质
senses.example: The meeting is of great significance.
senses.why: This is the basic importance sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的重性义项。

senses.title: Meaning
senses.definition: the meaning that something carries
senses.definitionCN: 某事物所承载的含义
senses.example: The discovery is of great significance to medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 这一发现对医学有重大意义。
senses.why: Something meaningful also matters.
senses.whyCN: 有意义的东西同时也重要。

intro.en: Significance comes from a Latin verb meaning to make signs.
intro.cn: significance 来自一个意为「做记号」的拉丁语动词。

items.en: Significare meant to show by signs.
items.cn: significare 意为用记号表明。

items.en: Significantia meant meaning.
items.cn: significantia 意为含义。

items.en: English borrowed the word through French.
items.cn: 英语经由法语借入这个词。

items.en: The sense of importance grew stronger.
items.cn: 「重要性」的含义变得更强。

items.en: Science gave it a statistical sense.
items.cn: 科学赋予它统计学的含义。

note.en: Significance is compared with similar-looking words and with words for importance.
note.cn: 把 significance 与形近词以及表示重要性的词作比较。

entries.definition: the meaning of a word or sign

normalIntro.en: Significance is the weight a thing carries.
normalIntro.cn: significance 是一件事所承载的分量。

normal.en: The discovery is of great significance to medicine.
normal.cn: 这一发现对医学有重大意义。

normal.en: The building has historical significance.
normal.cn: 这座建筑具有历史意义。

normal.en: They attach great significance to education.

normal.cn: 结果达到了统计显著性。

normal.en: The meeting is of great significance.

abstract.en: Significance is meaning with weight.
abstract.cn: 重要意义是有分量的含义。

abstract.en: Small events can carry large significance.
abstract.cn: 小事也能承载重大意义。

abstract.en: What we attend to gains significance.
abstract.cn: 我们关注的东西会变得重要。

examples.en: The discovery is of great significance to medicine.
examples.cn: 这一发现对医学有重大意义。

examples.en: The building has historical significance.
examples.cn: 这座建筑具有历史意义。

sensesIntro.en: Significance means importance or meaning.
sensesIntro.cn: significance 意为重要性或意义。

core.en: A mark whose meaning carries weight.
core.cn: 含义具有分量的记号。

branches.en: The meeting matters a great deal.
The finding carries meaning for medicine.
branches.cn: 这一发现对医学有意义。

branches.en: History gives the building weight.
branches.cn: 历史赋予这座建筑分量。

branches.en: Meaning and importance reinforce each other.
branches.cn: 含义与重要性彼此加强。
